video.title: AI Agencies Just Got Simple Enough for Anyone to Start

summary: Chris Koerner interviews Flo, the founder of Lindy, about its prompt-based agent builder and computer-use features. They discuss how AI agents could support agencies and automate sales, recruiting, customer support, creator workflows, and other business processes. The central business opportunity is to pair knowledge of a specific industry with the ability to build and monitor agents for its businesses. The guest demonstrates Lindy, so product claims and the host’s repeated affiliate promotion create a promotional conflict.

speakers.description: Lindy founder; surname is not stated in the transcript.

ideas.name: AI automation agency for small and medium-sized businesses
ideas.one_liner: Use low-cost agent tools to automate business processes for clients, with the agency combining industry knowledge and technical implementation.
ideas.business_model: Monthly retainer, one-time setup, or setup fee plus ongoing monthly fee.
ideas.customer: Small and medium-sized businesses; a successful agency is described as specializing in a particular industry or business function.
ideas.problem: Owners know they should use AI but do not know where to start, and may lack the time or technical skills to build agents.
ideas.offer: Understand a business's processes, create and monitor agents that automate selected tasks, and adapt them as the client’s needs change.

pricing.model: Retainer, one-time fee, or setup plus ongoing monthly fee.

price_points.label: Host's general suggested setup or project range

pricing.notes: These are host-stated opportunity ranges, not verified prices from a named agency.

acquisition_channels.details: Flo says agencies often have existing networks and expertise in their own verticals. Specific customer-acquisition methods are not otherwise stated.

quote.text: each of them is an expert in their own vertical and each of them has their own existing network.
quote.speaker: Flo

ideas.delivery: The agency learns the client's processes, builds agents on a platform such as Lindy, and monitors and adjusts them. Flo says consultants are still needed to understand how agents should be deployed in a business and that setup takes time.
unit_economics_claims: The host suggests a monthly fee of $500 to $5,000, a one-time fee of $300 to $5,000, or an ongoing fee of $2 to $700 per month; these are not reported results.

acquisition.how: Referrals and the agency's own network are mentioned, but there is no demonstrated automated sales process. Automated unsolicited outreach to UK individuals and sole traders would require care under PECR.

onboarding.how: Agents can be created from prompts, but understanding a client's processes and confirming the workflow still require human work.

delivery.how: Agents can perform much of the configured process; the agency still needs to build, monitor, and refine them.

billing.how: Recurring or one-time billing could be handled by software, but no billing workflow is demonstrated.

support.how: Agents can handle routine tasks, but the agency remains responsible for exceptions, client questions, and monitoring.

uk_applicability.notes: The agency model can apply to UK businesses. It needs UK-specific privacy, data protection, and marketing compliance; unsolicited electronic marketing to individuals and sole traders is restricted under PECR.

risks: The offer depends on understanding a client's actual processes, not just generating an agent from a prompt.
Agents that act on refunds, customer data, or business systems need appropriate permissions and human checks.
The host's suggested prices are not verified agency results.
Cold electronic marketing to UK individuals and sole traders requires consent; cold email to limited companies is permitted subject to applicable rules.

onboarding.how: The firm must agree role requirements, client terms, and candidate standards with the employer.

delivery.how: Search and matching can be automated, but candidate quality, consent, screening, and interview decisions need human oversight.

support.how: Agents could check placement status and send follow-ups, but disputes and hiring decisions need human handling.

ideas.customer: Businesses receiving customer-support inquiries, including teams with internal refund tools.
ideas.problem: Support teams handle repetitive inquiries and may be unable to connect agents to internal tools through an API.
ideas.offer: Build an agent that interprets support requests, answers within defined rules, and uses browser-based tools to perform actions such as issuing refunds.
ideas.delivery: The host proposes an email-triggered refund workflow in Stripe. Flo describes customer-support teams using agents with computer use to log into internal tools and issue refunds. The example is a Lindy use case, not a priced agency service.

acquisition.how: No service customer-acquisition method is stated.

onboarding.how: The business must define support policies, identity checks, refund limits, permissions, and escalation rules.

delivery.how: Agents can answer routine queries and use internal tools, but refunds and account changes need safeguards and human review for exceptions.

billing.how: Could use recurring billing, but no pricing or billing method is stated.

support.how: Agents can handle routine inquiries, with human escalation for disputes, uncertain identity, or high-impact actions.

uk_applicability.notes: Customer support automation can be used by UK businesses. Refund handling must follow the client's policy and UK consumer rights; personal data and payment access need appropriate controls.

risks: An agent could issue an inappropriate refund or expose customer data if permissions are too broad.
Browser-based computer use may be less reliable than an approved integration and needs monitoring.
The transcript provides no pricing or measured customer-support results.

tactics.name: Sell expertise at the intersection of AI and a specific industry
steps: Choose an industry or function where you already understand the work.
Learn which processes and software cause the most friction for those businesses.
Pair that knowledge with the ability to build and monitor agents.
Explain the value in terms of the client's workflow rather than the novelty of AI.

quote.text: Few people live in the intersection of those two. And when you do like you can you can deliver a lot of very differentiated value.
quote.speaker: Flo

tactics.name: Show a prospect useful work before asking for a meeting
steps: Research the prospect and its public needs or active campaigns.
Prepare a small, relevant sample, such as matching candidates or a competitor-ad review.
Email the sample with a clear next step and a specific offer to provide more.
Follow UK PECR and data-protection rules when contacting the prospect.

quote.text: Because sales like this brings sales from here's what I can do for you to here's what I just did for you.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Use a small sample to demonstrate recruiting fit
steps: Read job descriptions from a company's careers page.
Extract role requirements such as skills, experience, and location.
Find a few candidates that appear to match.
Send a short example list and offer to provide more, with consent and lawful data handling.

quote.text: This is an example of like three leads that we found and we have their email address. We can reach out to them.
quote.speaker: Flo

tactics.name: Use customer-language prompts and iterate
steps: Describe the task in ordinary language, including the trigger, action, and information needed.
Give more context by dictating if that makes it easier to explain the workflow.
Review the agent's proposed plan and answer its clarification questions.
Run the workflow, then use follow-up prompts to correct errors or refine behavior.

quote.text: we actually recommend dictating it because you can give a lot more details when you dictate.
quote.speaker: Flo

tactics.name: Break complex workflows into specialized agents
steps: Split a large process into narrower tasks.
Assign agents to specialized tasks and define the information they pass to each other.
Keep the agents in one platform where their work can be monitored.
Review the overall workflow for failures and unintended actions.

quote.text: You can create agents that are specialized in certain tasks and you can get them to like talk to each other and and collaborate with each other.
quote.speaker: Flo

tactics.name: Build the offer around demonstrated social workload
steps: Identify repetitive comment or inbox tasks that the creator currently leaves undone.
Agree on moderation or response rules with the account owner.
Automate routine work and keep ambiguous or sensitive cases available for human review.
Measure workload and outcomes before making savings claims.

quote.text: you can offer this as a service for people that don't want to read all these toxic comments
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Turn lead-magnet comments into a repeatable response workflow
steps: Publish a post offering a useful template or resource to commenters.
Have the agent identify each commenter and try the permitted contact method.
If private messaging is unavailable, use an approved public response that invites the commenter to initiate contact.
Monitor replies and respect platform rules and UK marketing requirements.

quote.text: So, for example, five days ago, we posted this tweet, this comment on this post on on LinkedIn, and it's like, "I built this AI agent, you know, this is what it does.
quote.speaker: Flo

tactics.name: Research a brand before negotiating sponsorship
steps: Screen inbound sponsorship messages for a credible sender and relevant offer.
Research the brand and its apparent audience before replying.
Tailor the rate response to the brand and creator's audience fit.
Require creator approval before accepting terms or committing to deliverables.

quote.text: as you offer a number, you could also re research the brand first, right?
quote.speaker: Flo

tactics.name: Check contingency placements after introduction
steps: Record which candidates were introduced to each client and when.
Agree clear placement-fee terms before making introductions.
Use an appropriate follow-up process to confirm hiring outcomes.
Resolve discrepancies through the contract and human review rather than relying solely on a profile change.

quote.text: you can have another AI agent that checks every month the LinkedIn profiles of the candidates that you introduced to customers to see if they joined the customer.

lessons.lesson: Choose a niche where you understand the business problem, then add technical skill; the overlap can be more valuable than generic AI knowledge.

quote.text: Few people live in the intersection of those two. And when you do like you can you can deliver a lot of very differentiated value.

lessons.lesson: Customers value a concrete demonstration of work already done more than a generic promise of what a service might do.

lessons.lesson: Reduce the gap between the person who understands the business and the person who can change the automation; faster iteration can improve the solution.

lessons.lesson: A single platform for agents may simplify monitoring and coordination, especially when agents need to work together.

lessons.lesson: Technology adoption moves from early advantage to basic expectation and eventually to a disadvantage for those who do not adopt.

quote.text: at first you get an advantage if you adopt these technologies first and then at some point you were at a disadvantage if you haven't adopted these technologies.

lessons.lesson: Automated workflows should leave room for human judgment when handling sensitive, ambiguous, or consequential interactions.
